claim: Curated Mendelian / ClinVar-pathogenic germline evidence links the target gene to this disease (or a subtype or very similar disease), and it was published before the program entered Phase 2.
evidence_source: Hutton M et al. Association of missense and 5'-splice-site mutations in tau with the inherited dementia FTDP-17. Nature 1998;393:702-705 (includes R406W, a mutation whose carriers are often clinically diagnosed with AD)
stop_reason: The Phase 2 PERISCOPE-ALZ trial missed its primary endpoint (iADRS), and Lilly disclosed in October 2021 that it was ending zagotenemab development. Imaging biomarkers and plasma NfL showed no evidence of pharmacodynamic activity or disease modification.
outcome_summary:
Phase 2 entry confirmed: NCT03518073 (PERISCOPE-ALZ, Eli Lilly) is the only registered industry Phase 2 trial of zagotenemab (LY3303560) in Alzheimer disease. It started 2018-04-30, enrolled 360 people with early symptomatic AD and finished its primary completion on 2021-08-23.

The primary endpoint, change in iADRS, was not met. Mean change at 104 weeks was -13.72 for placebo versus -15.11 and -14.38 for the two zagotenemab doses, so neither dose was better than placebo. Secondary outcomes (ADAS-Cog13 and others) also showed no benefit. The Neurology 2024 publication states that zagotenemab did not significantly slow clinical progression and that imaging biomarkers and plasma NfL showed no evidence of pharmacodynamic activity or disease modification. Lilly announced the end of development in October 2021. No Phase 3 was started.

I coded this F2 (an adequately dosed antibody that gave no clinical benefit). F1 is a reasonable alternative, because the trial never showed downstream pharmacodynamic engagement of aggregated tau.

evidence.earliest_source: Hutton M et al. Association of missense and 5'-splice-site mutations in tau with the inherited dementia FTDP-17. Nature 1998;393:702-705 (includes R406W, a mutation whose carriers are often clinically diagnosed with AD)
evidence.notes: 1. Zagotenemab (LY3303560, Eli Lilly) is a humanized antibody against aggregated/conformational tau; target MAPT is correct. 'Decreases function' is a reasonable reading of neutralizing or clearing pathological tau, though the antibody does not lower normal tau function. 2. Alzheimer disease (MONDO:0004975) is the Phase 2 indication; mapping is sound. 3. Mendelian MAPT mutations (ClinVar/OMIM pathogenic) cause frontotemporal dementia with parkinsonism-17 / FTLD-tau (OMIM 600274), not Alzheimer disease, which has amyloid plus tau pathology and APP/PSEN1/PSEN2 as its Mendelian genes. Some MAPT mutations (e.g. R406W, V337M) produce an AD-like amnestic phenotype with tau filaments in the Alzheimer fold and are frequently diagnosed clinically as AD, so MAPT has Mendelian evidence for a closely related tauopathy dementia. Common-variant AD evidence at the MAPT 17q21.31 locus (e.g. Jun et al. 2016 Mol Psychiatry) is GWAS, not Mendelian. Hence partial: only if FTDP-17 counts as 'very similar' to AD. 4. The 1998 reports (Hutton; Poorkaj; Spillantini) predate the 2018 Phase 2 entry. 5. Not authored by Lilly. No data errors found.

failure_second.rationale: PERISCOPE-ALZ (NCT03518073, Lilly, start 2018-04-30, n=360, early symptomatic AD) missed its primary endpoint: iADRS change at 104 weeks was -13.72 placebo vs -15.11 (1400 mg) and -14.38 (5600 mg); the posterior probability of >=25% slowing was <0.01% in each arm. F1 is the alternative because central engagement of aggregated tau was never shown. Lilly ended development in 2021.

evidence_source: Hutton M et al., 'Association of missense and 5'-splice-site mutations in tau with the inherited dementia FTDP-17', Nature 1998 (PMID 9641683); also Poorkaj 1998 and Spillantini 1998
stop_reason: TAURIEL (prodromal-to-mild AD) showed no clinical efficacy on CDR-SB and no slowing of tau-PET accumulation, so its OLE was terminated. LAURIET (mild-to-moderate AD) met the ADAS-Cog11 co-primary but missed the ADCS-ADL co-primary, so the study was formally negative. outcome_summary:
The earliest industry Phase 2 trial of semorinemab (RO7105705/MTAU9937A) in AD is Genentech's TAURIEL, NCT03289143, in prodromal-to-mild AD (n=457), with an actual start of 2017-10-04, matching the pipeline date. CT.gov lists it as terminated during the open-label extension because the blinded portion 'did not show any evidence of clinical efficacy or modulation of accumulation of tau PET signal at any of the doses studied'; its primary endpoint was change in CDR-SB.

The second Phase 2, LAURIET (NCT03828747, moderate AD, start 2019-01-25), showed a 42.2% reduction in ADAS-Cog11 decline at week 49 (p=0.0008) but no effect on the co-primary ADCS-ADL. The Neurology publication calls the study negative on its prespecified co-primaries (AC Immune PR Aug 2021; Neurology 2023).

No Phase 3 started. On 2024-01-22 AC Immune announced it would regain global rights to semorinemab after Genentech/Roche ended the collaboration. The antibody had adequate exposure in the trials but did not slow clinical decline or tau-PET accumulation, consistent with F2 (biology did not translate); the lack of tau-PET modulation leaves some doubt over whether it engaged pathological tau in the brain.

evidence.earliest_source: Hutton M et al., 'Association of missense and 5'-splice-site mutations in tau with the inherited dementia FTDP-17', Nature 1998 (PMID 9641683); also Poorkaj 1998 and Spillantini 1998
evidence.notes:
1. Semorinemab (RO7105705/MTAU9937A, Genentech/AC Immune) is an anti-tau (MAPT) antibody that targets the N-terminus to neutralise extracellular tau. Target MAPT and action 'decreases function' are correct.
2. MONDO:0004975 Alzheimer disease is the correct mapping for the Phase 2 program (Tauriel, prodromal-to-mild AD, started around Oct 2017).
3. MAPT pathogenic germline variants are firmly Mendelian for frontotemporal dementia with parkinsonism-17 (FTDP-17) and other primary tauopathies (1998), not for Alzheimer disease. Mendelian AD genes are APP, PSEN1 and PSEN2.

Some MAPT mutations, such as R406W, cause an AD-like amnestic phenotype (reports from the 2000s; reviewed in PMID 29370822). ClinVar currently has only a single 'likely pathogenic' MAPT variant annotated to Alzheimer disease, a recent submission. Hence partial.
5. These sources are not by the sponsor (Genentech/Roche/AC Immune). No data errors found.

outcome_summary:
Phase 2 entry confirmed: HER2CLIMB (NCT02614794, Seagen/Cascadian), a randomized trial of tucatinib vs placebo with capecitabine and trastuzumab in HER2+ metastatic breast cancer, actual start 2016-01-28. Earlier industry tucatinib breast cancer studies (NCT02025192, NCT01983501) were Phase 1b.

claim: Before the program entered Phase 2, the FDA had approved a drug acting on the same target for this disease or a closely related one.

stop_reason: n/a (not stopped)
outcome_summary:
Gentuximab (GenSci-043) is Changchun GeneScience's anti-VEGFR2 monoclonal antibody, a ramucirumab-like agent. The earliest industry Phase 2 trial in this disease is NCT04053205, a Phase Ib/II study of gentuximab plus paclitaxel in advanced gastric/GEJ cancer. Its actual start was 2019-11-05, matching the pipeline date. It completed 2020-09 with 76 enrolled and no posted results. An earlier Phase 1 trial, NCT03313219 (2017), covered solid tumors.

The randomized, double-blind Phase 3 trial NCT05919381 began 2022-05-30, within 4 years of entry. Its primary endpoint is overall survival. The registry status is 'unknown' (last updated 2023-06), and no topline results have been posted or published. Chinese media reported in July 2026 that CDE had accepted GeneScience's marketing application for gentuximab injection. This is the first domestic VEGFR2 antibody filing in China, presumably for use with paclitaxel after first-line failure. A filing suggests the Phase 3 was positive, but I found no formal primary-endpoint disclosure, so I mark the endpoint not_reported.

claim: Before the program entered Phase 2, the FDA had approved a drug acting on the same target for this disease or a closely related one.
evidence_source: FDA approval of Benlysta (belimumab, anti-BLyS/TNFSF13B), BLA 125370, 9 March 2011, indicated for systemic lupus erythematosus (not rheumatoid arthritis)
stop_reason: n/a (approved in China by NMPA for MTX-inadequate-response moderate-to-severe RA, July 2024; not FDA-approved)
outcome_summary:
The earliest industry Phase 2 trial of telitacicept (RC18) in RA is NCT02882087, sponsored by RemeGen. ClinicalTrials.gov gives its start as October 2015, matching the 2015-10-01 pipeline date. It was terminated on 2019-02-25 because it could not recruit enough subjects ('Lack of trial population').

RemeGen started the Phase 3 trial NCT03016013 on 2017-03-29. It was a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in 479 Chinese patients with moderate-to-severe RA and an inadequate response to methotrexate, and it was completed 2022-12-29. The primary endpoint, ACR20 at week 24, was met: 60.0% on telitacicept 160 mg plus MTX versus 26.9% on placebo plus MTX (p<0.001). ACR50 (21.4% vs 5.9%) and radiographic non-progression on mTSS also favored telitacicept.

China's NMPA granted approval for RA (in combination with MTX) in July 2024. That makes RA the drug's second approved indication in China, after SLE in 2021; gMG was approved later. There is no FDA approval for RA. The program advanced within 4 years because a Phase 3 started in 2017.

evidence.earliest_source: FDA approval of Benlysta (belimumab, anti-BLyS/TNFSF13B), BLA 125370, 9 March 2011, indicated for systemic lupus erythematosus (not rheumatoid arthritis)
evidence.notes:
1. Telitacicept (RC18; RemeGen) is a TACI-Fc fusion protein. It neutralizes both BLyS/BAFF (TNFSF13B) and APRIL (TNFSF13), so the targets and 'decreases target function' are correct.
2. MONDO:0008383 (rheumatoid arthritis) is a sound mapping. The Phase 2 RA trial in TNF-inadequate responders (NCT02882087) started in October 2015, consistent with the recorded 2015-10-01 entry date.
3. Before 2015 the FDA had approved only one drug on either target: belimumab (anti-BLyS), in 2011, and only for SLE. No BLyS- or APRIL-targeting drug was FDA-approved for RA before 2015 or since.
4. The verdict is partial because the target-matched approval exists but is for SLE. SLE is a different systemic autoimmune rheumatic disease, not a subtype of RA, so whether the claim holds depends on how broadly 'closely related' is read. Under a strict reading (RA or an RA subtype only) the claim is not supported.
5. The source is a GSK/Human Genome Sciences approval, not RemeGen. No data errors found.

outcome.summary:
The earliest industry Phase 2 trial of telitacicept (RC18) in RA is NCT02882087, sponsored by RemeGen. ClinicalTrials.gov gives its start as October 2015, matching the 2015-10-01 pipeline date. It was terminated on 2019-02-25 because it could not recruit enough subjects ('Lack of trial population').

RemeGen started the Phase 3 trial NCT03016013 on 2017-03-29. It was a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in 479 Chinese patients with moderate-to-severe RA and an inadequate response to methotrexate, and it was completed 2022-12-29. The primary endpoint, ACR20 at week 24, was met: 60.0% on telitacicept 160 mg plus MTX versus 26.9% on placebo plus MTX (p<0.001). ACR50 (21.4% vs 5.9%) and radiographic non-progression on mTSS also favored telitacicept.

China's NMPA granted approval for RA (in combination with MTX) in July 2024. That makes RA the drug's second approved indication in China, after SLE in 2021; gMG was approved later. There is no FDA approval for RA. The program advanced within 4 years because a Phase 3 started in 2017.

claim: Before the program entered Phase 2, the FDA had approved a drug acting on the same target for this disease or a closely related one.
error_source: none (earlier osteoarthritis trials of adalimumab were academic; Phase 2 entry is dated by the first industry trial)
evidence_source: No FDA approval of a TNF inhibitor for osteoarthritis exists. Closest: etanercept (Enbrel, BLA 103795) approved 1998-11-02 for rheumatoid arthritis, and adalimumab (Humira, BLA 125057) approved 2002-12-31 for RA. RA is a different disease from OA (autoimmune vs degenerative).
stop_reason: The OKINADA proof-of-concept trial in inflammatory knee OA missed its primary endpoint (OMERACT-OARSI response at week 16: 30.0% adalimumab vs 25% placebo, p=0.90) and secondary pain endpoints. The investigators concluded that short-term anti-TNF therapy gives no clinically meaningful improvement in OA symptoms, and no further industry development followed.
outcome_summary:
The industry-sponsored Phase 2 trial of adalimumab in osteoarthritis is OKINADA, NCT02471118, sponsored by CARE Arthritis Ltd (CT.gov class INDUSTRY) with AbbVie as collaborator. It enrolled 62 patients at 11 Canadian sites, with an actual start of 2015-03 (month precision only) and completion in 2021-03. Earlier adalimumab OA trials (Stanford 2005, Ghent 2006, Alberta 2008, AP-HP Phase 3 in hand OA 2008) were academic-sponsored and predate the entry, so this is the earliest industry Phase 2.

Results (ACR Convergence 2022; EULAR 2022 OP0229): the primary endpoint, OMERACT-OARSI responder rate at week 16, was not met (9/30 [30.0%] vs 7/28 [25%], p=0.90). KOOS pain improvement of 20% or more was 36.7% vs 24.1% (p=0.30). There were no new safety signals. The authors concluded that short-term TNF inhibition gives no clinically meaningful benefit in knee OA with effusion.

No Phase 3 of adalimumab in OA started after 2015, and adalimumab has no OA approval. Adalimumab 40 mg every two weeks is a validated, well-exposed regimen, so the failure is the biology (TNF inhibition) not translating into benefit: F2. [Correction by the second coder: the primary endpoint was 30.0% vs 24.1% responders, p=0.62 (EULAR 2022 abstract); p=0.90 was the KOOS pain >=50% comparison.]

evidence.earliest_source: No FDA approval of a TNF inhibitor for osteoarthritis exists. Closest: etanercept (Enbrel, BLA 103795) approved 1998-11-02 for rheumatoid arthritis, and adalimumab (Humira, BLA 125057) approved 2002-12-31 for RA. RA is a different disease from OA (autoimmune vs degenerative).
evidence.notes:
1. Adalimumab is an anti-TNF monoclonal antibody, so target TNF and action 'decreases function' are correct.
2. MONDO:0005178 osteoarthritis matches the OA trials (knee OA trial OKINADA started March 2015; hand OA trials).
3. No TNF-acting drug has ever been FDA-approved for osteoarthritis. Anti-TNF approvals cover RA, psoriatic arthritis, ankylosing spondylitis, JIA, Crohn's, UC, psoriasis and HS. RA is an autoimmune synovitis and OA is a degenerative joint disease, so they are not 'closely related' in mechanism. If 'closely related' were read as 'any arthritis', the 1998 etanercept RA approval would count. Under the rule as written the claim is not supported.
4. The FDA approval documents are not sponsor-authored in the sense asked. Humira's own RA approval is by the drug's sponsor (Abbott/AbbVie), but it does not establish an OA approval.
DATA ERROR: The recorded Phase 2 entry of 2015-03-01 is not the earliest Phase 2 of adalimumab in OA. Earlier trials include NCT00185562 (Stanford pilot, Phase 2, started 2005-06) and NCT00686439 (Univ. of Alberta, Phase 1/2, started 2008-06). The conclusion does not change: anti-TNF RA approvals (1998) predate both dates, and there is still no OA approval.

failure_second.rationale: OKINADA (NCT02471118; lead sponsor CARE Arthritis Ltd, industry class; start 2015-03; n=62; 11 Canadian sites) tested adalimumab 40 mg every two weeks in knee OA with clinical effusion. The primary OMERACT-OARSI responder endpoint at week 16 was not met: 30.0% vs 24.1%, p=0.62 per the EULAR 2022 OP0229 abstract (the first coder's 25%/p=0.90 slightly misquotes it; p=0.90 belongs to the KOOS pain >=50% comparison). claim: Before the program entered Phase 2, the FDA had approved a drug acting on the same target for this disease or a closely related one.
evidence_source: FDA approval of Cosentyx (secukinumab), BLA 125504 (Novartis), 21 Jan 2015, for moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis
stop_reason: The PRELUDE proof-of-concept study did not meet its PoC criteria in any of the three cohorts (cutaneous, mucosal, lichen planopilaris), and no further development in lichen planus followed
outcome_summary:
Phase 2 entry confirmed: Novartis PRELUDE (NCT04300296), a randomized, placebo-controlled PoC basket trial of secukinumab 300 mg Q4W in lichen planus, actual start 2020-07-27, n=111, primary completion 2021-11-16. It is the only industry trial of secukinumab in LP on CT.gov.

Primary endpoint (IGA <=2 at week 16, Bayesian analysis): CLP 44.0% vs 58.2% on placebo (posterior difference -13.9); MLP 37.5% vs 23.1% (+14.1, 95% CrI -17.0 to 40.7); LPP 37.6% vs 30.9% (+6.5). Bärtschi/Novartis et al., BJD 2024, report that the PoC criteria were not met in any cohort, with numerical signals in MLP and LPP and no response in CLP. Safety was consistent with the known profile.

No Phase 3 trial had started by 2024-07-27, and none appears since. Secukinumab is an approved, well-characterized drug with known adequate exposure, so the miss reflects IL-17A biology that did not translate into LP benefit (F2). Subtype heterogeneity (a possible F3 element) is noted by the authors.

evidence.earliest_source: FDA approval of Cosentyx (secukinumab), BLA 125504 (Novartis), 21 Jan 2015, for moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis
evidence.notes:
1. Secukinumab is a human IgG1 monoclonal antibody that neutralizes IL-17A, so IL17A with a decrease in function is right.
2. Lichen planus (MONDO:0006572) is a sound mapping for the investigator/Novartis lichen planus trial (PRELUDE, NCT04300296).
3. No IL-17A drug was FDA-approved for lichen planus before 2020-07-27, or since. The approved IL-17A antagonists, secukinumab (2015) and ixekizumab (2016), are approved for psoriasis, psoriatic arthritis and axial spondyloarthritis.
4. Psoriasis and lichen planus are both T-cell-mediated papulosquamous skin diseases with IL-17/Th17 involvement, but they are clinically and histologically distinct entities. Calling psoriasis 'closely related' is arguable, so the claim is partial rather than yes.
5. The earliest qualifying approval is the program drug's own approval, sponsored by Novartis, so it is sponsor-authored.
6. No data error found.

failure_second.rationale: PRELUDE (NCT04300296, Novartis, start 2020-07-27, n=111) was a PoC basket of secukinumab 300 mg Q4W vs placebo. claim: Before the program entered Phase 2, the FDA had approved a drug acting on the same target for this disease or a closely related one.
evidence_source: FDA approval of MS Contin (morphine sulfate extended-release, NDA 019516, 1987), a mu-opioid (OPRM1) agonist for chronic moderate-to-severe pain. Later examples include OxyContin (NDA 020553, Dec 1995) and Ultram ER (tramadol ER, 2005) for chronic pain
stop_reason: Not publicly stated. The NIDA-funded Phase 2 in diabetic neuropathic pain completed in 2020-08 without posted or published results, and no Phase 3 followed. This fits a small company's financing or partnering limits (or an unpublished result), but there is no confirmation.
outcome_summary:
NCT03664921 ('Omnitram Safety and Efficacy in the Treatment of Diabetic Neuropathy') is an industry Phase 2 trial sponsored by Syntrix Biosystems. Its conditions are diabetic neuropathies, neuropathic pain and chronic pain. The actual start was 2018-11-15, matching the pipeline date, and it completed 2020-08-17 with 55 enrolled. It was a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover with a numeric pain scale primary endpoint after 4 weeks, funded by NIDA. Syntrix's press release of 2019-03-20 announced dosing of the first cohort. ClinicalTrials.gov has no posted results (last update 2021-09), and I found no publication or press release of the outcome.

Syntrix's published human data are the healthy-volunteer experimental-pain trials in J Pain 2019;20:1218 (Zebala et al.). They showed analgesia equivalent to tramadol that does not depend on CYP2D6. Those trials do not test the chronic pain indication. After that the company registered only a 2021 Phase 1 PK/food-effect study (NCT04683926). No Phase 3 or NDA exists, so the program did not advance within 4 years. Because the Phase 2 outcome and the reason for stopping are undisclosed, I code the failure as unknown.

evidence.earliest_source: FDA approval of MS Contin (morphine sulfate extended-release, NDA 019516, 1987), a mu-opioid (OPRM1) agonist for chronic moderate-to-severe pain. Later examples include OxyContin (NDA 020553, Dec 1995) and Ultram ER (tramadol ER, 2005) for chronic pain
evidence.notes:
1. Desmetramadol (O-desmethyltramadol, M1) is the active mu-opioid receptor agonist metabolite of tramadol, so OPRM1 agonism is correct. It also inhibits norepinephrine reuptake, mainly through the (-)-enantiomer; this is a secondary pharmacology not captured by the single target.
2. Many FDA-approved OPRM1 agonists are labeled for chronic pain, e.g. extended-release morphine (1987) and oxycodone (1995), with the long-term opioid labeling 'pain severe enough to require daily, around-the-clock, long-term opioid treatment'. So the same target and action had approval for chronic pain long before 2018.
3. Disease mapping is partial. MONDO:0024317 'chronic pain syndrome' is a broad term, and opioid approvals are for chronic pain generally rather than a distinct 'chronic pain syndrome'. I could not confirm whether the 2018 Phase 2 studied chronic or acute pain.
4. The sponsor is Syntrix Biosystems, so none of these approvals are sponsor-authored.
5. I could not verify the Phase 2 date (2018-11-15) in ClinicalTrials.gov under 'desmetramadol'. The only Syntrix registration I found is a 2021 Phase 1. Treat the date as unconfirmed, not as an error.

claim: Before the program entered Phase 2, the FDA had approved a drug acting on the same target for this disease or a closely related one.
evidence_source: FDA accelerated approval of Balversa (erdafitinib, pan-FGFR1-4 kinase inhibitor), NDA 212018, 12 April 2019, for locally advanced or metastatic urothelial carcinoma with susceptible FGFR3 or FGFR2 alterations after platinum chemotherapy
stop_reason: In FIDES-02 (NCT04045613), derazantinib monotherapy failed its ORR primary endpoint in FGFR1-3-altered urothelial carcinoma: combined ORR 8% (95% CI 3-20%) in substudies 1 and 5 (n=49), median PFS 2.1 months. The study closed early with low enrollment. Basilea returned the derazantinib license to Merck & Co. (termination notice 2022-06-27, effective 2022-12-27), and Merck chose not to pursue development.
outcome_summary:
The earliest industry Phase 2 trial of derazantinib in urothelial carcinoma is FIDES-02, NCT04045613, a Phase 1b/2 multi-substudy trial of derazantinib alone and with atezolizumab, sponsored by Basilea. ClinicalTrials.gov records its actual start as 2019-08-02, matching the pipeline date. It was completed 2022-10-04. The earlier Phase 1/2 trial NCT01752920 was a basket study in solid tumors, not a urothelial-specific trial.

Results were presented at ASCO GU 2023. Derazantinib monotherapy missed the ORR primary endpoint both in chemotherapy-pretreated patients (substudy 1) and in the 300 mg BID cohort (substudy 5). failure_second.rationale: FIDES-02 (NCT04045613) started 2019-08-02 and completed 2022-10-04. Monotherapy ORR was 9.4% for 300 mg QD in substudy 1 and 5.9% for 200 mg BID in substudy 5 (not 300 mg BID as the first coder wrote), pooled about 8%, so the benchmark was missed. With the target validated in this setting, the likeliest cause is inadequate FGFR engagement by the molecule. Basilea's license return (F8) followed the negative data and is secondary.

claim: Before the program entered Phase 2, the FDA had approved a drug acting on the same target for this disease or a closely related one.
evidence_source: None: no FDA approval of an IL-1beta-targeting drug for sarcoidosis or a closely related granulomatous lung disease. The earliest IL-1beta approvals are rilonacept (Arcalyst, 2008, CAPS) and canakinumab (Ilaris, BLA 125319, 2009-06-17, CAPS), both for autoinflammatory periodic fever syndromes.
stop_reason: The randomized placebo-controlled Phase 2 missed its primary endpoint (week-24 change in % predicted FVC: -1.90 on canakinumab vs +0.52 on placebo). Only minor secondary signals (6MWT, air trapping). Novartis did not develop it further in sarcoidosis.
outcome_summary:
NCT02888080 (Novartis) is the only industry trial of canakinumab (ACZ885) in pulmonary sarcoidosis on ClinicalTrials.gov: a Phase 2, randomized, placebo-controlled study of 300 mg s.c. monthly for 6 months, n=40, actual start 2016-12-19 (matching the pipeline date), completed 2019-03-04, results posted 2020-03.

The primary endpoint, change from baseline to week 24 in % predicted FVC, was not met. The canakinumab arm declined by a mean of 1.90 (SD 3.91) and the placebo arm rose by 0.52 (SD 3.37). The FDG-PET SUVmax change at week 12 was -4.48% vs +4.07% with very wide SDs. Reviews describe the trial as negative, with modest 6MWT and air-trapping improvements and good tolerability. No Phase 3 or approval followed.

Failure code F2: canakinumab is a well-characterized IL-1β antibody given at an established dose, so exposure and engagement are not in question. Blocking IL-1β did not improve lung function in this population. The small size (n=40) is a caveat, but the direction of the primary endpoint went against the drug.

3. FDA approvals before 2016-12 of drugs acting on IL-1beta: canakinumab for CAPS (2009) and for TRAPS, HIDS/MKD and FMF (September 2016); rilonacept, an IL-1alpha/beta trap, for CAPS (2008); anakinra targets IL1R1 rather than IL1B. 4. earliest_year/predates_entry refer to the nearest IL-1beta approval (2009 CAPS), which does not satisfy the disease condition. The approval holder for canakinumab is Novartis, the program's sponsor; the field is set to 'no' because no qualifying source exists.
5. No data errors found.

claim: Before the program entered Phase 2, the FDA had approved a drug acting on the same target for this disease or a closely related one.
evidence_source: None before entry. The nearest is FDA approval of latanoprostene bunod (VYZULTA, NDA 207795) for open-angle glaucoma/ocular hypertension on 2 Nov 2017. It is a nitric-oxide-donating prostaglandin analogue that acts on sGC only indirectly, through NO, and it postdates entry.
stop_reason: No IOP-lowering efficacy compared with vehicle in the Phase 1/2 trial (Part 3), and ocular hyperemia limited the dose. No further trials are registered.
outcome_summary:
Phase 2 entry confirmed: NCT02743780 (Alcon/Novartis) was a 3-part first-in-human Phase 1/2 trial of topical MGV354, an sGC activator, in patients with ocular hypertension or glaucoma. It started 2016-03-02 and finished its primary completion on 2016-09-20, with 191 participants. It is the only registered trial of MGV354.

The Part 3 primary endpoint, change in mean diurnal IOP at day 8, was not met. MGV354 lowered IOP by -0.6 mm Hg versus -1.1 mm Hg for vehicle (CI -0.7 to 1.7) (Stacy et al., Am J Ophthalmol 2018;192:113-123, PMID 29802818). The dose was the maximum tolerated dose, and MGV354 produced conjunctival and ocular hyperemia 'consistent with its pharmacology', which is evidence of on-target vasodilatory activity. A later Novartis metabolism study (Xenobiotica 2021, PMID 32662714) found no species difference in metabolism that could explain the lack of efficacy. Development did not continue.

I coded this F2 (on-target activity present, no IOP benefit). F5 is a possible alternative, because the dose was capped by on-target hyperemia.

evidence.earliest_source: None before entry. The nearest is FDA approval of latanoprostene bunod (VYZULTA, NDA 207795) for open-angle glaucoma/ocular hypertension on 2 Nov 2017. It is a nitric-oxide-donating prostaglandin analogue that acts on sGC only indirectly, through NO, and it postdates entry.
evidence.notes: 1. MGV354 (Novartis) is a selective, topical, heme-independent soluble guanylate cyclase activator. sGC alpha1/beta1 (GUCY1A1+GUCY1B1) is the correct target, and 'increases function' is correct. 2. Ocular hypertension (MONDO:0006875) matches the Phase 1/2 study in ocular hypertension/open-angle glaucoma; mapping is sound. 3. Before March 2016 the only FDA-approved drug acting directly on sGC was riociguat (Adempas, 2013, sGC stimulator), approved for PAH and CTEPH, not an ocular indication. Organic nitrates and nitroprusside activate sGC through NO but are approved for cardiovascular uses. No sGC-acting drug was FDA-approved for ocular hypertension or glaucoma before entry. Latanoprostene bunod (Nov 2017) postdates entry and acts mainly on the FP receptor. Vericiguat (2021) is cardiovascular. 4. Claim not supported. No data errors found in target, action or disease.

Hyperemia consistent with sGC-mediated vasodilation shows that the drug was active at the target in ocular tissue, yet IOP did not fall, so the biology did not translate in humans. F5 is less apt because there was no efficacy for the toxicity to offset.

claim: Before the program entered Phase 2, the FDA had approved a drug acting on the same target for this disease or a closely related one.
evidence_source: FDA approval of fostamatinib disodium (Tavalisse, NDA 209299), a SYK inhibitor, on 2018-04-17 for chronic immune thrombocytopenia (ITP) - not for RA
stop_reason: The global Phase 2 in active RA (inadequate response to MTX/anti-TNF) missed its primary endpoint, change in DAS28-hsCRP at week 12 (topline January 2021). Safety was clean. Oscotec said a higher dose might improve efficacy, but it has run no further RA trial and has focused cevidoplenib on immune thrombocytopenia.
outcome_summary:
The earliest industry Phase 2 trial of cevidoplenib (SKI-O-703, an oral SYK inhibitor) in RA is Oscotec's NCT04057118, a randomized double-blind placebo-controlled dose-ranging study (100/200/400 mg BID, n=163), with an actual start of 2019-03-20 (matching the pipeline date) and completion on 2020-10-13. The other cevidoplenib Phase 2, NCT04056195, is in ITP.

In January 2021 Korea Biomedical Review reported that the trial missed its primary endpoint (DAS28-hsCRP change at week 12) and showed no significant effect on remission, with no serious toxicity. Oscotec said it expected 'to improve efficacy by increasing the dose' and would consider further testing, but CT.gov lists no later RA trial; later cevidoplenib trials are ITP, ADME and bioequivalence studies, and the drug received FDA orphan designation for ITP.

Failure code F1 is a judgement call. SYK inhibition is clinically validated in RA (fostamatinib), and the sponsor attributed the miss to insufficient dose, so the likeliest explanation is inadequate exposure or engagement at the doses tested; no target-engagement data were reported. Status 'stopped' is inferred from the absence of RA activity since 2021; no formal discontinuation announcement was found.

evidence.earliest_source: FDA approval of fostamatinib disodium (Tavalisse, NDA 209299), a SYK inhibitor, on 2018-04-17 for chronic immune thrombocytopenia (ITP) - not for RA
evidence.notes:
1. Cevidoplenib (SKI-O-703, a prodrug of SKI-O-592; Oscotec/Genosco) is a selective oral SYK inhibitor, so target SYK and action 'decreases function' are correct.
2. MONDO:0008383 rheumatoid arthritis matches the Phase 2 trial NCT04057118 (active RA, Oscotec, actual start 2019-03-20), which matches the recorded date.
3. Before 2019-03-20 the only FDA-approved SYK-acting drug was fostamatinib, approved 2018-04-17 for chronic ITP. Fostamatinib had been tested in RA Phase 3 (OSKIRA), but its RA filing was never approved. ITP and RA are both autoantibody/Fc-receptor-driven autoimmune diseases with a shared SYK mechanism, but they are not closely related clinical diseases. So the same target was approved pre-entry, but only for a different autoimmune indication: partial.
4. Fostamatinib (Rigel) is not the sponsor's drug. No data errors found.

failure_second.rationale: Posted results for NCT04057118 (n=163) show the week-12 change in DAS was -0.95 on placebo against -0.91, -1.06 and -1.15 at 100, 200 and 400 mg BID: a high placebo response and only a shallow dose trend, with no significant difference. Eligibility required inadequate response to anti-TNF agents. Oscotec attributed the miss mainly to the refractory population ('many of the recruited patients had serious RA') and saw promise in less severe RA. Fostamatinib also failed its primary endpoint in TNF-inadequate responders while working in MTX-inadequate responders, so a wrong-population explanation has clinical precedent. The sponsor also mentioned a dose increase, so F1 is a plausible alternative, but no PK or engagement data were reported. Confidence is low.

adjudication.rationale: NCT04057118 (start 2019-03-20, n=163) enrolled RA patients with inadequate response to csDMARDs and anti-TNF biologics. Posted week-12 DAS28-hsCRP changes were -0.95 placebo vs -0.91/-1.06/-1.15 at 100/200/400 mg BID: no separation and only a shallow dose trend. Oscotec's stated explanation (Korea Biomedical Review, Jan 2021) was the patient population ('many of the recruited patients had serious RA'), and there is direct class precedent: fostamatinib failed in TNF-inadequate responders while showing efficacy in MTX-inadequate responders. No PK or target-engagement data were reported, so an exposure explanation (F1, the sponsor's secondary dose-increase remark) cannot be excluded, but the refractory-population explanation is better supported by the sponsor's attribution and class precedent. Confidence low-moderate.

claim: Before the program entered Phase 2, the FDA had approved a drug acting on the same target for this disease or a closely related one.
evidence_source: FDA approval of Entyvio (vedolizumab), BLA 125476 (Takeda), 20 May 2014, for moderately-to-severely active ulcerative colitis and Crohn's disease
stop_reason: The Phase 2b PROPEL trial was stopped for futility in June 2018 at the interim analysis (65 patients), driven by an unusually high placebo remission rate (~24%). Blinded endoscopy re-reads later showed CRO read errors and gave efficacy signals. Protagonist nonetheless replaced PTG-100 with the more potent second-generation alpha4beta7 antagonist PN-943 rather than resuming PTG-100 in UC
outcome_summary:
Phase 2 entry confirmed: PROPEL (NCT02895100, Protagonist), a Phase 2b trial of the oral gut-restricted alpha4beta7 peptide PTG-100 in moderate-to-severe UC, start December 2016. The trial was planned for 240 patients and enrolled 98 (actual).

In June 2018 the independent DMC halted the trial for futility at the planned interim analysis, which found an unusually high placebo clinical remission rate (~24%, about 4x historical). CT.gov lists the trial as terminated, 'futility-based outcome'. A re-read by the CRO's subcontractor and a fully blinded re-read by Robarts found errors in a subset of the original endoscopy reads, and Protagonist said the corrected final data showed efficacy signals that supported further development.

PTG-100 never entered Phase 3 for UC. In 2019 Protagonist moved its UC effort to PN-943, citing superior potency and target engagement over PTG-100, which effectively ended PTG-100 in UC; later PTG-100 activity was an investigator-sponsored celiac Phase 1. The proximate cause of the failure to advance was trial execution: erroneous endoscopy reads inflated placebo remission and triggered the futility stop (F7). The final decision was a portfolio switch to PN-943 (an F8 element).

evidence.earliest_source: FDA approval of Entyvio (vedolizumab), BLA 125476 (Takeda), 20 May 2014, for moderately-to-severely active ulcerative colitis and Crohn's disease
evidence.notes:
1. PTG-100 is Protagonist's oral, gut-restricted peptide antagonist of alpha4beta7 integrin, so ITGA4+ITGB7 with a decrease in function is right.
2. Ulcerative colitis (MONDO:0005101) is right; the Phase 2b PROPEL trial (NCT02895100) was in moderate-to-severe UC.
3. Vedolizumab, an anti-alpha4beta7 monoclonal antibody, was approved for UC on 2014-05-20, before the Phase 2 entry. Natalizumab (anti-alpha4) was also approved for Crohn's disease in Jan 2008.
4. ClinicalTrials.gov gives the PROPEL study start as December 2016, which matches the recorded 2016-12-01 entry. Protagonist announced the start in January 2017.
5. The approval belongs to Takeda, not Protagonist.
6. No data error found.

claim: Human germline genetics established, before the program entered Phase 2, a mechanism for this target in this disease that the drug's action opposes (e.g. risk variants raise the gene's function and the drug lowers it, or loss-of-function variants are protective and the drug lowers function, or loss-of-function causes the disease and the drug raises function).
evidence_source: Koenig M et al., Cell 1987;50:509-17 (PMID 3607877), complete DMD cDNA cloning with deletions in patients; Hoffman EP, Brown RH, Kunkel LM, Cell 1987;51:919-28 (PMID 3319190), dystrophin absent in DMD; OMIM 310200
stop_reason: n/a (not stopped). The confirmatory trial failure puts continued accelerated approval in question.
outcome_summary:
The earliest industry Phase 2 trial is NCT02740972 (NS Pharma, 'Safety and Dose Finding Study of NS-065/NCNP-01 in Boys With DMD'). Its actual start was 2016-12, matching the pipeline date, and it completed 2018-03 with 16 enrolled. Its primary endpoints were safety and dystrophin production by Western blot, and the dystrophin increase supported accelerated approval. An earlier Phase 1 trial, NCT02081625 (NCNP, Japan), started in 2013.

The program advanced within 4 years. The Phase 3 confirmatory trial RACER53 (NCT04060199) started 2020-04-14, and FDA granted accelerated approval to Viltepso on 2020-08-12 on the basis of dystrophin expression. On 2024-05-27 NS Pharma and Nippon Shinyaku reported that RACER53 (77 boys, 48 weeks, 80 mg/kg weekly vs placebo) missed its primary endpoint. Time-to-stand velocity was not significantly different from placebo, and no new safety signals appeared. The approval remains in place pending regulatory discussions, and the open-label RACER53-X extension (NCT04768062) and a Phase 4 registry (NCT04687020) are ongoing.

evidence.earliest_source: Koenig M et al., Cell 1987;50:509-17 (PMID 3607877), complete DMD cDNA cloning with deletions in patients; Hoffman EP, Brown RH, Kunkel LM, Cell 1987;51:919-28 (PMID 3319190), dystrophin absent in DMD; OMIM 310200
evidence.notes:
1. Viltolarsen (NS-065/NCNP-01) is a phosphorodiamidate morpholino oligomer that induces exon 53 skipping in DMD pre-mRNA, restoring the reading frame and producing truncated, functional dystrophin. DMD as target and 'increases function' are correct.
2. DMD is caused by X-linked loss-of-function (frameshift/null) DMD variants, established by positional cloning in 1986-87 and by the finding that dystrophin is absent in patients (1987). ClinVar holds thousands of pathogenic DMD variants. LoF causes the disease and the drug raises function, so P2 is met.
3. The disease mapping to MONDO:0010679 is exact. The drug applies only to the roughly 8% of patients with exon-53-amenable deletions.
4. The sources are academic (Kunkel lab) and are not authored by Nippon Shinyaku/NS Pharma or NCNP.
5. The Phase 2 entry 2016-12 is consistent with the North American Phase 2 (NCT02740972). The Japanese Phase 1 began in 2013. No data errors found.

The earliest industry Phase 2 trial of rezvilutamide (SHR3680) in prostate cancer is NCT02691975 (Jiangsu HengRui), a Phase 1/2 study in mCRPC with actual start 2016-04-12, matching the pipeline date. Because it is Phase 1/2 rather than pure Phase 2, the confirmation rests on the Phase 2 component.

HengRui started the Phase 3 CHART trial (NCT03520478) on 2018-05-30. CHART met its co-primary endpoints, rPFS and OS, vs bicalutamide+ADT in high-volume mHSPC (Gu et al., Lancet Oncol 2022;23:1249-1260). The NMPA approved rezvilutamide in June 2022. evidence.earliest_source: Irvine RA et al., Cancer Res 1995;55:1937-1940 (AR CAG/GGC microsatellite alleles associated with prostate cancer); directional evidence in Giovannucci E et al., PNAS 1997;94:3320-3323 (shorter AR CAG repeats, which give higher AR transactivation, associated with higher prostate cancer risk). evidence.notes:
1. Rezvilutamide (SHR3680, Jiangsu Hengrui) is a second-generation androgen receptor antagonist, so target AR and action 'decreases function' are correct.

3. Germline evidence with a direction: candidate-gene studies from 1995-1997 reported that shorter AR exon-1 CAG repeats, which raise AR transcriptional activity, carry higher prostate cancer risk. This is the opposite of the drug's AR-lowering action. Later meta-analyses found the association weak and inconsistent, so the evidence does not firmly establish the mechanism.
4. GWAS identified an Xq12 risk locus about 70 kb from AR (Kote-Jarai 2011, Nat Genet; rs5919432). It predates 2016 and implicates the AR region, but it does not show the effect direction on AR function or that AR is the effector gene.
5. Complete AR loss of function (androgen insensitivity) prevents normal prostate development. That supports AR dependence of prostate tissue but is not a cancer-risk genetic mechanism in itself.
6. Overall: germline evidence implicates AR and points in a direction the drug opposes, but it is not robustly established, hence 'partial'. All sources predate Phase 2 entry, and none is authored by Hengrui.
7. No data errors found, apart from the Phase 1/2 note in item 2.

Phase 2 entry is only partly confirmed. NCT03899467 (Kintor, GT0918-US-1002) is a US multicentre, randomized, open-label Phase 2 trial in mHSPC/mCRPC after abiraterone or enzalutamide. It started 2019-05-30, matching the pipeline date. Its primary endpoint was safety and tolerability plus RP2D selection, and no efficacy hypothesis was tested (only 2/28 and 1/29 patients had a 50% or greater PSA decline at 12 weeks). However, Kintor had already run a Phase 2 in China (data presented at ASCO GU 2021) and had started a Phase 3 in China in September 2018, so the US trial is not the earliest industry Phase 2.

The program advanced under the stated definition. Kintor's 2024 interim report describes write-offs from suspending pruxelutamide trials. No approval followed, so the program is effectively stopped despite advancing. These China Phase 3 trials are registered on chinadrugtrials.cn, not ClinicalTrials.gov, so the start dates come from company and broker disclosures.

outcome_summary:
Lexanersen (WVE-120102) is Wave Life Sciences' allele-selective (SNP2) antisense oligonucleotide. Its first industry trial in HD is PRECISION-HD2, NCT03225846, a Phase 1b/2a randomized placebo-controlled intrathecal study (n=88), with an actual start of 2017-07-17, matching the pipeline date. CT.gov lists it as terminated for 'Lack of efficacy', as is the OLE NCT04617860 (start 2019-09-24). Because the trial was Phase 1b/2a, the Phase 2 entry is confirmed with that caveat.

The registered primary endpoints were safety and tolerability counts (TEAEs, severe and serious TEAEs, withdrawals), so 'met or not met' does not strictly apply; primary_endpoint is 'na'. The efficacy readout that mattered was pharmacodynamic. On 2021-03-30 Wave reported no dose response and no statistically significant change in CSF mHTT versus placebo up to 32 mg monthly, and ended development of WVE-120102 and WVE-120101 (Wave PR; NeurologyLive; HDBuzz).

The molecule never showed target engagement (mHTT lowering) at the doses tested, which is a molecule-level failure: F1. Wave then moved to a new chemistry (WVE-003).

evidence.earliest_source: The Huntington's Disease Collaborative Research Group, 'A novel gene containing a trinucleotide repeat that is expanded and unstable on Huntington's disease chromosomes', Cell 1993 (PMID 8458085)
evidence.notes:
1. Lexanersen sodium is WVE-120102 (Wave Life Sciences), an allele-selective stereopure antisense oligonucleotide. It targets an HTT SNP in phase with the expanded CAG allele and lowers mutant HTT mRNA and protein. Target HTT and action 'decreases function' are correct; strictly, it lowers the mutant allele selectively.
2. MONDO:0007739 Huntington disease is correct. PRECISION-HD2 (NCT03225846, Phase 1b/2a) actual start 2017-07-17 matches the recorded date (the trial is Phase 1/2).
3. HD is an autosomal dominant disease caused by germline CAG expansion in HTT (1993). The genetics show a toxic gain-of-function of the mutant allele: dominant inheritance, homozygotes not clinically distinct from heterozygotes (Wexler 1987), and repeat length correlating with age at onset. HTT haploinsufficiency (Wolf-Hirschhorn deletions; heterozygous knockout mice) does not cause HD. Lowering mutant HTT opposes this mechanism, so the claim is supported, well before 2017.
4. The source is not by Wave. No data errors found.

evidence_source: Weber S et al. Muscarinic acetylcholine receptor M3 mutation causes urinary bladder disease and a prune-belly-like syndrome. Am J Hum Genet 2011;89:668-674 (PMC3213389; ClinVar RCV000022466 pathogenic; OMIM 100100)
stop_reason: The Phase 2a PoC trial missed its primary endpoint (change in catheterized PVR showed no difference from placebo), and no further development is registered
outcome_summary:
Phase 2 entry confirmed: Astellas' Phase 2a PoC trial of the M3 positive allosteric modulator ASP8302 in underactive bladder (NCT03702777), actual start 2018-11-20, n=135, primary completion 2020-04-28. The only other ASP8302 trial on CT.gov is a Phase 1 in healthy Japanese volunteers.

Primary endpoint (change from baseline in PVR after standardized filling, PVRc2, at week 4): median -40.0 mL with ASP8302 vs -35.0 mL with placebo, difference -5.0 mL, p=0.960 (van Till et al., Neurourol Urodyn 2022). Secondary signals appeared in males (higher Qmax and detrusor pressure at Qmax, fewer incontinence episodes). AEs were similar (33.3% vs 31.4%).

No Phase 3 or further trials are registered, and the program is treated as discontinued. The primary miss with only subgroup or secondary signals fits F2, biology that did not translate. Direct human target-engagement evidence is limited, so F1 cannot be fully excluded, and the male-only signals hint at a population element (F3).

evidence.earliest_source: Weber S et al. Muscarinic acetylcholine receptor M3 mutation causes urinary bladder disease and a prune-belly-like syndrome. Am J Hum Genet 2011;89:668-674 (PMC3213389; ClinVar RCV000022466 pathogenic; OMIM 100100)
evidence.notes:
1. ASP8302 is Astellas's positive allosteric modulator of the M3 muscarinic receptor, which augments cholinergic detrusor contraction. CHRM3 with an increase in function is right.
2. The program's indication is underactive bladder/detrusor underactivity (NCT03702777). 'Urinary bladder disorder' (MONDO:0006026) is a broad parent term that contains it, but it is less specific than ideal, so the mapping is partial.
3. Weber et al. 2011 found a homozygous frameshift/truncating CHRM3 variant (c.1173_1184delinsT, p.Pro392fs) in a consanguineous family. Affected members had congenital bladder malformation, a large poorly contracting bladder, and in some a prune-belly-like syndrome. ClinVar lists the variant as pathogenic. Beaman et al. (Clin Genet 2019) later added a homozygous missense CHRM3 family, but that postdates entry.
4. Loss of CHRM3 function causes bladder disease with failed detrusor contraction, and the drug raises M3 function. That is the opposing mechanism P2 asks for.
5. Caveat: the evidence is a single family with a congenital, recessive phenotype, whereas the drug's target population is adult acquired underactive bladder. The direction is clear but the phenotypic match is not exact.
6. Weber et al. are academic (Hildebrandt/Woolf groups), not Astellas.
7. No data error found beyond the broad disease term.

evidence_source: Riordan JR et al., Science 1989;245:1066-73 (PMID 2475911); Kerem B et al., Science 1989;245:1073-80 (PMID 2570460); Rommens JM et al., Science 1989;245:1059-65 (PMID 2772657), identification of CFTR and the loss-of-function deltaF508 mutation in CF
stop_reason: Inhaled CFTR mRNA was safe and well tolerated, but the multiple-ascending-dose cohorts showed no pattern of ppFEV1 improvement (second interim, March 2021). The early single-dose FEV1 signal from 2019 did not replicate. Translate Bio shifted to a next-generation CF candidate before Sanofi acquired it in 2021, and MRT5005 was dropped.
outcome_summary:
NCT03375047 (RESTORE-CF) is a Phase 1/2 trial of nebulized MRT5005 in adults with CF. It was initiated by Translate Bio and is now listed under Sanofi. The actual start was 2018-05-10, matching the pipeline date, and it completed 2022-03-15 with 42 enrolled and results posted. Its primary endpoint, treatment-emergent and serious adverse events, was met: dosing was generally safe and tolerated. On efficacy, the 2019 interim showed ppFEV1 increases after a single dose, but the March 2021 second interim found 'no pattern of increases in ppFEV1' in the multiple-dose groups.

No Phase 3 followed. Translate Bio redirected to a next-generation CF mRNA/LNP candidate, Sanofi bought the company in 2021, and the CF Foundation lists MRT5005 as discontinued. I code F1: no study showed that the molecule delivered enough functional CFTR protein to the airway epithelium. There was no lung-expression or CFTR-function biomarker, and the sponsor's move to a next-generation delivery candidate points to a delivery or expression problem with this molecule, not a failure of CFTR biology (which CFTR modulators validate). F2 is less likely.

outcome.summary:
NCT03375047 (RESTORE-CF) is a Phase 1/2 trial of nebulized MRT5005 in adults with CF. It was initiated by Translate Bio and is now listed under Sanofi. The actual start was 2018-05-10, matching the pipeline date, and it completed 2022-03-15 with 42 enrolled and results posted. Its primary endpoint, treatment-emergent and serious adverse events, was met: dosing was generally safe and tolerated. On efficacy, the 2019 interim showed ppFEV1 increases after a single dose, but the March 2021 second interim found 'no pattern of increases in ppFEV1' in the multiple-dose groups.

No Phase 3 followed. Translate Bio redirected to a next-generation CF mRNA/LNP candidate, Sanofi bought the company in 2021, and the CF Foundation lists MRT5005 as discontinued. I code F1: no study showed that the molecule delivered enough functional CFTR protein to the airway epithelium. There was no lung-expression or CFTR-function biomarker, and the sponsor's move to a next-generation delivery candidate points to a delivery or expression problem with this molecule, not a failure of CFTR biology (which CFTR modulators validate). F2 is less likely.

failure_second.rationale: RESTORE-CF (NCT03375047, Ph1/2, start 2018-05-10, n=42) met its safety primary endpoint, but the March 2021 second interim showed no pattern of ppFEV1 increases with repeat dosing. No airway CFTR expression or function was shown. CFTR restoration is clinically validated by modulators, so the failure most plausibly reflects inadequate delivery/expression by this mRNA-LNP rather than the biology. Translate Bio shifted to next-generation LNP candidates, and MRT5005 was discontinued after the Sanofi acquisition.

Phase 2 entry confirmed: NCT03289143 (TAURIEL, Genentech) was the first industry Phase 2 trial of semorinemab. It started 2017-10-04 and enrolled 457 people with prodromal-to-mild AD. The CDR-SB primary endpoint was not met (p=0.51-0.61 for the three doses vs placebo). The trial was terminated during its open-label extension because the blinded portion showed no clinical efficacy or modulation of tau-PET accumulation.

A second Phase 2, LAURIET (NCT03828747, started 2019-01-25, n=272 with moderate AD), met the ADAS-Cog11 co-primary (p=0.0008) and reduced CSF and plasma tau biomarkers, which shows target engagement. It missed the ADCS-ADL co-primary (p=0.52) and the secondary efficacy endpoints. A Phase 3 decision was deferred and never made. I coded this F2: engagement was shown in LAURIET but did not translate into consistent clinical benefit.

evidence.earliest_source: Hutton M et al. Association of missense and 5'-splice-site mutations in tau with the inherited dementia FTDP-17. Nature 1998;393:702-705 (gain-of-toxic-function/aggregation-promoting MAPT mutations; established for FTDP-17, not AD)
evidence.notes: 1. Semorinemab (RO7105705, Genentech/AC Immune) is a humanized IgG4 anti-tau antibody against the N-terminus, meant to bind extracellular tau and block its spread. Target MAPT is correct, and 'decreases function' is a fair reading of neutralizing pathological tau. 2. Alzheimer disease (MONDO:0004975) is the indication of the Phase 2 TAURIEL (prodromal-to-mild AD, started Oct 2017); mapping is sound. 3. Germline genetics establishes that dominant missense and splice MAPT mutations raise tau aggregation propensity or the 4R:3R ratio and cause FTDP-17/FTLD-tau. A drug lowering pathological tau opposes that mechanism. Some of these mutations (R406W, V337M) give an AD-like amnestic phenotype. For AD itself, though, germline genetics did not establish a MAPT mechanism before 2017: AD's Mendelian genes are APP/PSEN1/PSEN2, and evidence linking the MAPT H1/H2 haplotype to AD was inconsistent. The 17q21.31 association reported by Jun et al. (Mol Psychiatry 2016) is a GWAS signal with unresolved causal gene and direction. Hence partial: direction-consistent germline mechanism for a related tauopathy, not for AD. 4. The 1998 source predates the 2017-10-04 entry. 5. Not authored by Genentech/Roche or AC Immune. No data errors found.

outcome_summary:
The earliest industry Phase 2 trial of zagotenemab (LY3303560, an anti-aggregated-tau antibody) in AD is Lilly's PERISCOPE-ALZ, NCT03518073, in early symptomatic AD (n=360), with an actual start of 2018-04-30 (matching the pipeline date) and completion on 2021-10-25. Earlier LY3303560 studies (NCT02754830, NCT03019536) were Phase 1.

The primary endpoint, change on iADRS, was not met. The Neurology 2024 publication reports no significant slowing of clinical progression and no evidence of pharmacodynamic activity or disease modification on imaging biomarkers or plasma NfL. Lilly disclosed the miss and the end of development in its Q3 2021 earnings materials (Alzforum).

No Phase 3 started. Failure code F2: the drug was dosed systemically at the planned exposures and the anti-tau hypothesis did not translate into benefit. The absence of any biomarker pharmacodynamic signal means F1 (central engagement never shown) is a reasonable alternative.

evidence.earliest_source: Hutton M et al., Nature 1998 (PMID 9641683): MAPT mutations cause FTDP-17 tauopathy (gain of aggregation-prone tau). For AD specifically, the MAPT-region GWAS signal (Jun G et al., Mol Psychiatry 2016, PMID 25778476) gives no clear direction of effect.
evidence.notes:
1. Zagotenemab (LY3303560, Eli Lilly) is a humanised antibody against aggregated/conformational tau (derived from MC-1). Target MAPT and action 'decreases function' (reduces pathological tau) are correct.
2. MONDO:0004975 Alzheimer disease is correct for the Phase 2 trial in early symptomatic AD (PERISCOPE-ALZ, NCT03518073), started around April 2018.
3. Human genetics shows MAPT mutations cause a dominant tau-aggregation neurodegeneration (FTDP-17, 1998), which supports reducing pathological tau. But that is a different disease from AD. Many FTDP-17 mutations reduce tau's microtubule binding while increasing its aggregation, so the direction of 'function' is mixed.
4. In AD itself, germline genetics place tau downstream of amyloid (APP/PSEN). MAPT H1/H2 haplotype and region associations with AD are weak and inconsistent (Jun 2016 found a locus near MAPT in APOE e4-negative subjects, attributed partly to KANSL1/other genes) and do not establish a direction of effect. So germline genetics had not established, before 2018, a mechanism for MAPT in AD that the drug opposes. Support comes only by extrapolation from a similar tauopathy: partial.
5. These sources are not by Lilly. No data errors found.

outcome_summary:
Phase 2 entry confirmed: Biogen's PASSPORT (251PP301, NCT03068468), a trial of gosuranemab (BIIB092, anti-N-terminal tau) in PSP, actual start 2017-06-01, n=490. Earlier trials were Phase 1 (SAD NCT02294851, MAD NCT02460094).

Primary endpoint: change in PSPRS at week 52 was 10.4 with gosuranemab vs 10.6 with placebo, difference -0.2, p=0.85 (CT.gov results). Dam et al., Nat Med 2021, report that gosuranemab sharply reduced unbound N-terminal tau in CSF, showing target engagement, but had no effect on clinical progression. Biogen terminated PASSPORT and its open-label extension (NCT02658916) with the reason 'primary endpoint was not met; further development of gosuranemab in PSP will not be pursued'.

No Phase 3 trial followed. Target engagement was demonstrated without clinical benefit (F2). The later Alzheimer's Phase 2 (TANGO, NCT03352557) also failed.

evidence.earliest_source: Conrad C et al. Genetic evidence for the involvement of tau in progressive supranuclear palsy. Ann Neurol 1997;41:277-281; extended by Baker M et al. Hum Mol Genet 1999 (H1 haplotype) and by MAPT gain-of-function mutations in FTDP-17, including PSP-like phenotypes (Hutton et al. Nature 1998)
evidence.notes:
1. Gosuranemab (BIIB092, formerly BMS-986168/IPN007) is a humanized antibody against N-terminal extracellular tau (eTau) fragments. It is meant to neutralize and lower extracellular tau, so MAPT with a decrease in function is right, though it acts on a tau species rather than on MAPT expression.
2. Progressive supranuclear palsy (MONDO:0019037) is right.
3. Germline genetics: the MAPT H1 haplotype raises PSP risk (Conrad 1997; Baker 1999) and H2 is protective. The 2011 PSP GWAS (Hoglinger et al., Nat Genet) confirmed MAPT as the strongest locus. H1/H1c have been tied to higher MAPT and 4R-tau transcript expression. Dominant MAPT mutations (FTDP-17, Hutton 1998), some with a PSP phenotype, increase 4R tau or aggregation propensity, i.e. a toxic gain of function. Risk alleles raising tau burden is opposed by a drug that lowers tau.
4. Caveat: the functional mechanism of the H1 association is less firmly established than the association itself, and it is unproven that extracellular N-terminal tau is the pathogenic species. The genetic direction is still consistent with lowering tau.
5. The sources are academic (Conrad/Mayo, Baker/Hutton), not Biogen, BMS or iPierian.
6. No data error found.
